newsitem.title: GHANA: Ghana oil refinery fire kills two - state agency.
newsitem.headline: Ghana oil refinery fire kills two - state agency.

text.p: A fire at Ghana's state-owned Tema Oil Refinery on Friday killed two workers and caused extensive damage, Ghana's state news agency reported.
President Jerry Rawlings went to inspect the damage and was told by chief executive William Parker that it would cost over $10 million to repair, Ghana News Agency (GNA) said.
The plant has been closed for refurbishment since January and the fire began during a test run that started on Tuesday.
Ghana has had to import all its petroleum products during the shutdown. It was not clear if the reopening, planned for August, would be put back because of the fire.
Ghana News Agency said Parker had estimated there was enough fuel to last the country four to five weeks, and he said all necessary measures would be take to avoid shortages.
